references.text: Both passages emphasize Jesus' role as the one who has seen God and is the only one who has made him known, which is central to the dialogue where Jesus reveals his identity to those who have seen him.
Jesus says to Philip: 'Whoever has seen me has seen the Father', a direct parallel to the statement in John 9:37 that whoever speaks with the healed man is the one he has seen.
Here Jesus warns that they have never heard the Father's voice or seen his form, which contrasts with the healed man who has actually seen and heard Jesus, who is the image of the Father.
Jesus declares that whoever believes in him believes in the one who sent him, and whoever sees him sees the one who sent him, reflecting the identity confirmation found in 9:37.
